facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is earnings momentum: issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the nine months was USD 3,323 million against USD 2,565 million a year earlier, the issuer guides to USD 4,315 million to USD 4,415 million of adjusted EBITDA for 2026, and cash of USD 2,485 million exceeds principal due before the end of 2027. That reading would win if a twelve-month adjusted EBITDA near the guidance range were confirmed, because net leverage on that basis would sit well below the 7.73x reported ratio; it would fail if the USD 3,766 million due in 2028 proved hard to refinance. A full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA or the fourth-quarter 2025 release would let an adjusted twelve-month ratio be built and settle the question. rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Adjusted EBITDA is stated for quarter and nine-month periods only and for no full fiscal year, so adjusted leverage and adjusted interest cover for FY2024, FY2025 and the last twelve months to 2026-09-30 are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release or a full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA. - Total interest paid is not printed for nine months 2025 or nine months 2026, so the cash interest paid line for those periods and interest cover for the last twelve months are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the quarterly supplemental cash flow disclosure or the issuer's interest paid for the nine months. - Reported EBITDA is not stated by the issuer for FY2024 or FY2025 and is calculated from audited components, so those two ratios rest on a derived denominator. Severity: Low. Action: Replace the calculated figures if the issuer later states a reported full-year EBITDA. - No reported fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied, so no discrete fourth-quarter series exists and the fourth quarter could only be derived as the full year less nine months. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release. - Revolver availability and letters of credit at 2024-12-31 and at 2025-09-30 are not stated, so undrawn facilities and liquidity relative to debt are not established for FY2024 or nine months 2025. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the 2024 annual report. - No balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is supplied, so total debt, net debt and leverage at that date and the nine-month 2025 balance sheet column are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report. - The annual income statement and the cash flow statement print dashes for several lines, including goodwill impairments in FY2024, the third quarter of 2026, the third quarter of 2025 and nine months 2025, the gain on extinguishment of debt in the third quarter of 2026, financial leases at 2024-12-31 and some cash flow adjustments; they are recorded as not supplied rather than zero. Severity: Low. Action: Read a dash as nil only where the narrative confirms it. - Asset impairments appear as a separate line only in the annual income statement; in the quarterly statements they sit inside other expense, net, so the quarterly cells for that line are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: Use the release reconciliation of other expense, net if a quarterly figure is needed. - Income taxes paid are printed for the fiscal years only, so the nine-month cash tax figures are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the quarterly supplemental cash flow disclosure. - The lien, collateral and legal rank of the 14.00% second lien notes, with principal of USD 352 million, are not described in any filing, and the nature of USD 12 million of other debt is not described, so both are left out of the debt stack. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the 2022 indenture for the 14.00% notes and the schedule of other debt. - No filing states a single legal rank across the Bausch Health collateral pool and the Bausch + Lomb collateral pool, so the cumulative leverage in the debt stack across the two pools is a presentation aid and not a legal waterfall. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the intercreditor and security documents. - The Q3 release and the quarterly report differ by USD 14 million on interest allocated to debt premiums for nine months 2026, USD 144 million against USD 158 million, and the sources do not explain the difference. Severity: Low. Action: Ask the issuer to reconcile the two figures. - The Q3 release labels USD 20,168 million of principal as net of premiums, discounts and issuance costs, while the quarterly report shows it as principal and USD 20,637 million as the net carrying value, so the release label is not followed. Severity: Low. Action: Quote debt with the quarterly report labels. - The redemption price and accrued interest on the 8.5% notes due 2027 are not stated, so the effect of the 2026-11-30 redemption on net debt and the pro forma net leverage are not established. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the redemption notice. - The euro carrying value of the Bausch + Lomb floating rate notes is not printed because the filing shows the carrying value in US dollars only, USD 756 million. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the euro carrying value from the issuer. - Failed sale-leaseback obligations that Bausch + Lomb records within financial leases and non-current debt are not split, so Total Debt may include a small amount of lease-like obligations that cannot be separated. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the split from the issuer. - Organic revenue growth is stated by the issuer only for nine months 2026 in the sources read, and revenue and segment growth for nine months 2025 cannot be formed because nine-month 2024 revenue is not in the sources, so those cells are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the third-quarter 2025 release and the nine-month 2024 comparatives. - No floor is stated for the Bausch + Lomb revolver or the Bausch + Lomb refinancing term facility, so their floors are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the Bausch + Lomb credit agreement. - The closing date of the Bausch + Lomb acquisition of ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses is stated only as the fourth quarter of 2026, so its date in the adjustments table is not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the closing announcement. - Executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, the covenant step-up date and the reported covenant ratio values are not established and covenant headroom is not calculated. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the 2025 credit agreement and the indentures.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Management has used liability management repeatedly, and the record is mixed for creditors. The 2022 exchange cut principal by USD 2,469 million, or 44.14%, and was accounted for as a troubled debt restructuring; the 2025 refinancing retired USD 6,870 million of debt due between 2025 and 2028 into secured debt due 2030 to 2032; and the December 2025 exchange swapped USD 1,683 million of 2028 secured notes for USD 1,600 million of 2032 notes while moving more Bausch + Lomb shares into the borrower. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is operating momentum: Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb reported fourteen consecutive quarters of revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth, the issuer raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 4,315 million to USD 4,415 million, nine-month consolidated revenue rose USD 847 million, and cash covers the redemption of the 2027 notes. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the issuer's guidance looks conservative: it implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 992 million to USD 1,092 million against USD 1,350 million in the third quarter, Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb reports fourteen consecutive quarters of growth, and leverage on guided adjusted EBITDA is between 4.04x and 4.16x in every perimeter. If Xifaxan held through 2028, or generic entry were delayed, the 2028 maturities would be refinanced from a stronger base and the view would improve. It would worsen if generic entry came earlier than expected, if Salix volumes kept falling while prices reset, or if a further exchange or release of the pledged shares re-ranked claims. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Bausch Health Companies Inc. presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by earnings momentum, a cleared 2027 wall and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on Xifaxan, thin reported cover and a 2028 maturity wall. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and earnings releases support the requested Bausch Health credit snapshot with stated limits, but not a legal reading of covenants and liens, a market-value view or a position-size view, so those conclusions stay open for creditors. Coverage ends on 2026-10-28, which is 8 days before the as-of date, so later events are not covered.

The reporting entity is the consolidated group, which includes the approximately 87% owned Bausch + Lomb with its own debt, cash and revolver, so every balance and earnings figure needs a perimeter label. The third quarter quarterly report prints cash and debt for the two perimeters separately. The third quarter earnings release labels USD 20,168 million of principal as net of premiums, whereas the quarterly report shows USD 20,637 million as the net carrying value.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt was USD 18,152 million at 2026-09-30, 7.73x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA or 4.81x excluding the Q1 2026 goodwill impairment, so creditors remain exposed to a heavily levered structure that depends on continued refinancing access. Reported cash interest cover was 1.73x in FY2025, and cover for the last twelve months is not established because interim cash interest is not stated.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 319–320.

Cash of USD 2,485 million and undrawn facilities of USD 1,135 million exceed principal due before the end of 2027 of USD 716 million, but Bausch + Lomb holds USD 515 million of group cash and USD 666 million of the undrawn facilities, and neither is generally available to other group entities.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 131.
### Key findings

Reported net leverage rose from 6.23x at FY2025 to 7.73x at 2026-09-30 even though net debt fell by USD 1,356 million, because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell from USD 3,131 million to USD 2,347 million after the USD 1,426 million goodwill impairment booked in Q1 2026. The impairment is non-cash and does not change debt service, and without it net leverage is 4.81x against 5.95x at FY2025 on the same basis, so leverage on a cash-earnings basis is falling while the reported ratio overstates the burden.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6.

Net debt fell because cash rose by USD 1,176 million to USD 2,485 million while gross debt fell only USD 180 million, so the improvement came from cash generation rather than debt repayment. Operating cash flow was USD 1,714 million in the nine months against purchases of property, plant and equipment of USD 252 million, but it excludes USD 158 million of contractual interest that the issuer allocates to debt premiums and reports in financing, so free cash flow of USD 1,462 million is flattered by that amount.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 126.

Cover is thin: FY2025 reported EBITDA was 1.73x cash interest paid of USD 1,810 million, and cash interest exceeded income statement interest expense of USD 1,604 million by USD 206 million, partly because USD 276 million of interest paid on secured notes carried at a premium reduces the premium instead of expense. Income statement interest therefore understates the cash burden, and cover for the last twelve months is not established because the quarterly filing prints no total interest paid.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 319–320.

Maturities are light until 2028, with USD 15 million of principal due in the rest of 2026 and USD 701 million in 2027, then USD 3,766 million in 2028 and USD 1,667 million in 2029, rising to USD 4,123 million in 2030 and USD 3,896 million in 2031, so refinancing is the central risk once cash is used. The approximately USD 643 million of 8.5% notes due 2027 are scheduled for redemption on 2026-11-30 from cash on hand, and the effect on net debt and pro forma net leverage is not established because the redemption price and accrued interest are not stated.
Basis: calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76.

Of principal debt of USD 20,168 million, USD 5,065 million sits at Bausch + Lomb, so Bausch Health itself carries USD 15,103 million against cash of USD 1,973 million, and the Bausch Health maintenance covenant excludes Bausch + Lomb earnings and net debt. Consolidated ratios therefore blend two credit groups with separate collateral and separate cash.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128.

Reported EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated here from audited components because no source states it, and adjusted EBITDA is stated only for quarter and nine-month periods, such as USD 3,323 million for nine months 2026, so adjusted leverage on a twelve-month basis is not established.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 24.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is earnings momentum: issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the nine months was USD 3,323 million against USD 2,565 million a year earlier, the issuer guides to USD 4,315 million to USD 4,415 million of adjusted EBITDA for 2026, and cash of USD 2,485 million exceeds principal due before the end of 2027. That reading would win if a twelve-month adjusted EBITDA near the guidance range were confirmed, because net leverage on that basis would sit well below the 7.73x reported ratio; it would fail if the USD 3,766 million due in 2028 proved hard to refinance. A full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA or the fourth-quarter 2025 release would let an adjusted twelve-month ratio be built and settle the question.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42.
### Limitations
- Full-year adjusted EBITDA and nine-month total interest paid are not stated, so adjusted leverage and last-twelve-month interest cover are not established.
- Reported EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated from audited components rather than stated by the issuer, and no reported fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2.
- Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 and any balance sheet at 2025-09-30 are not supplied, so liquidity and debt trends cover FY2025 and 2026-09-30 only.

- The lien and legal rank of the 14.00% second lien notes are not described in any filing and the notes are left out of the debt stack; executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.

- Consolidated debt and cash blend Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb, whose collateral pools and cash are separate, and the debt stack gives each pool first-priority debt the same rank without a legal ranking across the pools.

## Gaps

- Adjusted EBITDA is stated for quarter and nine-month periods only and for no full fiscal year, so adjusted leverage and adjusted interest cover for FY2024, FY2025 and the last twelve months to 2026-09-30 are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release or a full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA.

- Total interest paid is not printed for nine months 2025 or nine months 2026, so the cash interest paid line for those periods and interest cover for the last twelve months are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the quarterly supplemental cash flow disclosure or the issuer's interest paid for the nine months.

- Reported EBITDA is not stated by the issuer for FY2024 or FY2025 and is calculated from audited components, so those two ratios rest on a derived denominator. Severity: Low. Action: Replace the calculated figures if the issuer later states a reported full-year EBITDA.

- No reported fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied, so no discrete fourth-quarter series exists and the fourth quarter could only be derived as the full year less nine months. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release.

- Revolver availability and letters of credit at 2024-12-31 and at 2025-09-30 are not stated, so undrawn facilities and liquidity relative to debt are not established for FY2024 or nine months 2025. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the 2024 annual report.

- No balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is supplied, so total debt, net debt and leverage at that date and the nine-month 2025 balance sheet column are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report.

- The annual income statement and the cash flow statement print dashes for several lines, including goodwill impairments in FY2024, the third quarter of 2026, the third quarter of 2025 and nine months 2025, the gain on extinguishment of debt in the third quarter of 2026, financial leases at 2024-12-31 and some cash flow adjustments; they are recorded as not supplied rather than zero. Severity: Low. Action: Read a dash as nil only where the narrative confirms it.

- Asset impairments appear as a separate line only in the annual income statement; in the quarterly statements they sit inside other expense, net, so the quarterly cells for that line are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: Use the release reconciliation of other expense, net if a quarterly figure is needed.
- Income taxes paid are printed for the fiscal years only, so the nine-month cash tax figures are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the quarterly supplemental cash flow disclosure.

- The lien, collateral and legal rank of the 14.00% second lien notes, with principal of USD 352 million, are not described in any filing, and the nature of USD 12 million of other debt is not described, so both are left out of the debt stack. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the 2022 indenture for the 14.00% notes and the schedule of other debt.

- No filing states a single legal rank across the Bausch Health collateral pool and the Bausch + Lomb collateral pool, so the cumulative leverage in the debt stack across the two pools is a presentation aid and not a legal waterfall. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the intercreditor and security documents.

- The Q3 release and the quarterly report differ by USD 14 million on interest allocated to debt premiums for nine months 2026, USD 144 million against USD 158 million, and the sources do not explain the difference. Severity: Low. Action: Ask the issuer to reconcile the two figures.

- The Q3 release labels USD 20,168 million of principal as net of premiums, discounts and issuance costs, while the quarterly report shows it as principal and USD 20,637 million as the net carrying value, so the release label is not followed. Severity: Low. Action: Quote debt with the quarterly report labels.

- The redemption price and accrued interest on the 8.5% notes due 2027 are not stated, so the effect of the 2026-11-30 redemption on net debt and the pro forma net leverage are not established. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the redemption notice.

- The euro carrying value of the Bausch + Lomb floating rate notes is not printed because the filing shows the carrying value in US dollars only, USD 756 million. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the euro carrying value from the issuer.

- Failed sale-leaseback obligations that Bausch + Lomb records within financial leases and non-current debt are not split, so Total Debt may include a small amount of lease-like obligations that cannot be separated. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the split from the issuer.

- Organic revenue growth is stated by the issuer only for nine months 2026 in the sources read, and revenue and segment growth for nine months 2025 cannot be formed because nine-month 2024 revenue is not in the sources, so those cells are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the third-quarter 2025 release and the nine-month 2024 comparatives.

- No floor is stated for the Bausch + Lomb revolver or the Bausch + Lomb refinancing term facility, so their floors are not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the Bausch + Lomb credit agreement.

- The closing date of the Bausch + Lomb acquisition of ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses is stated only as the fourth quarter of 2026, so its date in the adjustments table is not established. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the closing announcement.

- Executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, the covenant step-up date and the reported covenant ratio values are not established and covenant headroom is not calculated. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the 2025 credit agreement and the indentures.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Bausch Health Companies Inc.
## Request

Business and governance review for Bausch Health Companies Inc. (issuer id bhc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, operating model, transactions, governance and sponsor-behaviour evidence in the seven supplied filings and releases, with amounts in USD millions unless stated.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors rely on a concentrated franchise and a layered group: Xifaxan supplied 21.55% of FY2025 revenue with generic entry expected in 2028, and the Bausch + Lomb stake behind the newest secured debt sits outside the older notes' guarantor group.
Basis: calculation K1; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40

No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed, so outside support cannot be assumed. Management has repeatedly extended maturities through exchanges and refinancings that moved priority to creditors of the financing subsidiary 126NumberCo, yet its 2026 actions, a USD 643 million note redemption from cash and a USD 50 million buyback aimed at dilution, favour debt reduction over distributions.
### Key findings

Profit comes from two engines of unequal quality. Salix earned 47.34% of nine-month 2026 segment profit on 26.79% of revenue, and Bausch + Lomb earned 27.04% on 48.25%, so group earnings rest on a US specialty franchise with a known loss of exclusivity and on a subsidiary whose cash is generally not available to other group entities.
Basis: calculation K4; calculation K5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 127

Xifaxan is the largest single exposure and its protection is eroding. It earned USD 2,212 million, 21.55% of FY2025 revenue and 85.80% of Salix revenue, while the negotiated Medicare price applies from 2027-01-01, the issuer expects generic competition in 2028 and the FDA has given final approval to a Teva generic whose launch date is not stated. The failure of the follow-on formulation's Phase 3 trials in January 2026 removed the replacement product and led to a USD 1,426 million goodwill impairment, leaving USD 1,733 million of Salix goodwill on the balance sheet.

Basis: calculation K1; calculation K2; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

Salix growth is price-led, so the profit gain depends on price holding. Nine-month 2026 Salix revenue rose USD 343 million, built from USD 504 million of net realized pricing and USD 12 million from discontinued products, less USD 173 million of lost volume, after the company exited high-rebate channels in the second half of 2025.
Basis: calculation K7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 123

Customer concentration is high and so is dependence on one market. Three wholesalers took 48% of FY2025 revenue and the United States 59.79%, so a distribution dispute would reach receivables and rebate accruals quickly; product rebate accruals alone were USD 1,377 million at 2026-09-30.
Basis: calculation K10; calculation K11; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 343; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

No sponsor or controlling shareholder is disclosed, so support from an owner cannot be assumed. Ten directors signed the annual report, but ownership, independence and related-party detail is incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied; letter agreements dated 2025-05-20 with two named shareholders are listed without their terms, a director nomination agreement ended on 2025-08-14, and a shareholder rights plan with a 20% threshold was adopted on 2025-04-14 and ratified on 2025-10-07.

Management overlap with Bausch + Lomb sharpens a conflict that matters to creditors. The chief executive became chairman of the Bausch + Lomb board in August 2026 and its interim chief executive on 2026-10-12, after the former Bausch + Lomb chief executive left with a separation payment of about USD 75 million, and the issuer itself flags the conflict risk. Because 68.28% of the Bausch + Lomb shares the group holds are pledged, and dividends above USD 50 million or sale proceeds must prepay the 126NumberCo secured debt, any separation or monetization of the stake would route value to those secured creditors first.

Management has used liability management repeatedly, and the record is mixed for creditors. The 2022 exchange cut principal by USD 2,469 million, or 44.14%, and was accounted for as a troubled debt restructuring; the 2025 refinancing retired USD 6,870 million of debt due between 2025 and 2028 into secured debt due 2030 to 2032; and the December 2025 exchange swapped USD 1,683 million of 2028 secured notes for USD 1,600 million of 2032 notes while moving more Bausch + Lomb shares into the borrower. Against that, the company repurchased USD 602 million of 2026 notes at close to par in August 2025 and announced redemption of USD 643 million of 2027 notes from cash. Non-guarantor subsidiaries produced 57.40% of nine-month revenue, so unsecured holders sit behind both secured claims and subsidiary liabilities.

Basis: calculation K15; calculation K16; calculation K17; calculation K18; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 293; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 130

Capital allocation is cautious on distributions and moderate on acquisitions. No dividend was declared in 2023, 2024 or 2025 and none is planned; the USD 50 million repurchase authorized on 2026-10-24 equals 2.01% of cash and is meant to offset dilution from management awards; recent deals were small, at USD 84 million for DURECT, USD 87 million for the China distributor and USD 85 million agreed by Bausch + Lomb, but management says larger deals in core areas are under review, which would compete with debt reduction.

Basis: calculation K20; calculation K21; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 132; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1

Reporting quality is a strength and creditor-level legal detail is the gap. The auditor has served since 2012, internal control over financial reporting was assessed effective at 2025-12-31 and covenant compliance is stated at 2026-09-30, but the executed indentures, the proxy statement and related-party terms are not supplied, so restricted-payment capacity and unrestricted-subsidiary capacity cannot be tested.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is operating momentum: Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb reported fourteen consecutive quarters of revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth, the issuer raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 4,315 million to USD 4,415 million, nine-month consolidated revenue rose USD 847 million, and cash covers the redemption of the 2027 notes. Bausch + Lomb revenue grew 7% in the third quarter and supplies 25.54% of guided adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint, so the stake is also a source of value. This view would be wrong if generic rifaximin entry slipped beyond 2028 or if Bausch + Lomb were separated with debt sized to each company. It would harden if a further exchange re-ranked claims, if pledged shares were released to other lenders or if generic entry came before 2028, and the proxy statement and executed indentures would settle control, independence and capacity.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation K12; calculation K22; calculation K20
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, shareholders with large stakes and related-party terms are not established, and the conclusion that no controlling holder exists could change if one is found.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 199

- The two shareholder letter agreements and the rights plan are listed or summarized without detail, so whether either holder influences board seats or capital decisions is not established, and the control conclusion is limited to the absence of a disclosed controlling holder.

- Teva's settlement terms and any launch date for generic rifaximin are not supplied, so the 2028 date rests on the issuer's expectation, and an earlier launch would bring forward the loss of Xifaxan earnings.
- Nine-month Xifaxan revenue is not stated, so concentration is measured on FY2025 and could be higher or lower now.
- The reason the stake in Bausch + Lomb moved from about 88% to about 87% is not stated, and Bausch + Lomb's share count is not supplied, so ownership is shown as the issuer states it at each date.

- The executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so the capacity to designate unrestricted subsidiaries, release the pledged shares or make restricted payments is read from the notes only, and the creditor-alignment view could harden or soften once the documents are read.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The group's largest recent debt transaction was the April 2025 refinancing at 126NumberCo, an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary: a USD 500 million revolver due 2030 that is undrawn, a USD 3,000 million term loan due October 2030 and USD 4,400 million of 10.00% secured notes due April 2032, secured on a first lien over 126NumberCo's assets including the pledged Bausch + Lomb shares. The proceeds repaid the 2027 term loan and redeemed USD 6,870 million of notes and term debt that matured between 2025 and 2028, which the issuer says extended maturities to the period 2030 to 2032.
Basis: calculation K18; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

In December 2025 the company and 126NumberCo exchanged USD 797 million of June 2028 secured notes and USD 886 million of 11.00% notes due 2028 for USD 1,600 million of new 10.00% notes due 2032 that form one series with the April 2025 notes, and moved further Bausch + Lomb shares into 126NumberCo. The issuer treated the exchange as a modification, not a troubled debt restructuring, and USD 803 million and USD 888 million of the old notes remain outstanding.
Basis: calculation K17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 284

Bausch + Lomb refinanced on its own credit. On 2025-06-26 it added a USD 800 million revolver due 2030, a USD 2,325 million term loan due 2031 and EUR 675 million of floating-rate secured notes due 2031 to repay its 2027 debt, and in January 2026 it replaced its 2028 and 2031 term loans with a USD 2,802 million term loan due 2031, of which USD 2,788 million was outstanding at 2026-09-30. These facilities are secured by Bausch + Lomb assets, so its USD 5,065 million of debt ranks ahead of the shares the parent holds.

Acquisitions were small: DURECT Corporation for USD 84 million plus milestones of up to USD 350 million, the China aesthetics distributor for about USD 87 million, and Bausch + Lomb purchases of about USD 75 million for manufacturing equipment, about USD 33 million for two businesses and about USD 85 million agreed on 2026-10-08 and expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. The debt table at 2026-09-30 shows no new Bausch Health issue in 2026; the changes were a lower term loan balance and the Bausch + Lomb refinancing.

On 2026-10-28 the company announced it will redeem all USD 643 million of its 2027 senior notes on 2026-11-30 from cash on hand, and on 2026-10-24 its board authorized a USD 50 million share repurchase program; the issuer states it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30.
Basis: calculation K20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

## Gaps
- The proxy statement is not supplied, so directors' independence, holders with large stakes, related-party terms and pay are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

- The executed indentures and 2025 credit agreement are not supplied, so capacity to designate unrestricted subsidiaries, release the pledged shares or make restricted payments is read from the notes only. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the indentures and the 2025 credit agreement.

- Teva's settlement terms and any launch date for generic rifaximin are not supplied, so the 2028 entry date rests on the issuer's expectation. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the settlement terms or a later filing that states the entry date.
- The terms of the letter agreements with Carl C. Icahn and John Paulson are not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the 8-K exhibits dated 2025-05-21.
- Nine-month Xifaxan revenue and product-level revenue other than Xifaxan are not stated. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain product revenue disclosures.
- Bausch + Lomb's shares outstanding are not supplied, so the change from about 88% to about 87% cannot be explained. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain Bausch + Lomb's own quarterly report.

- Intercompany arrangements between Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb beyond the master separation agreement are not described. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the exhibits to the master separation agreement.

- The outcome of the Luxembourg tax appeal, an assessment of EUR 271.7 million excluding interest on which no reserve is recorded, is pending. Severity: Medium. Action: Track the judgment expected within 90 days of the 2026-10-15 hearing.
- The participation rate in the 2022 and December 2025 exchanges and the terms offered to non-participants are not stated. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the exchange offer documents.

- No document dated after 2026-10-28 is supplied, so the issue of the redemption notice and any later management or ownership change is not evidenced. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain filings dated after 2026-10-28.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Bausch Health Companies Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit review for Bausch Health Companies Inc. (issuer id bhc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated credit view built from the financial foundation, the business and governance review and the seven supplied filings and releases, in USD millions unless stated.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

The credit is stretched but financeable for a year: earnings are improving and the 2027 wall is nearly cleared, yet dependence on one drug and USD 3,766 million due in 2028 leave creditors reliant on refinancing before generics arrive.
Basis: calculation M6; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Reported net leverage was 7.73x at 2026-09-30 on net debt of USD 18,152 million, or 4.81x without the non-cash goodwill impairment and 4.16x on guided adjusted EBITDA. Pro forma net debt is USD 18,227 million after the separation payment dated 2026-10-12 and USD 18,237 million after the Bausch + Lomb acquisition, whose date is not stated, giving 7.77x in each case; the effect of the redemption dated 2026-11-30 is not established.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M3; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

Earnings and cash flow are improving fast, which is the main support. Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 3,323 million against USD 2,565 million a year earlier and operating cash flow was USD 1,714 million against USD 905 million, and the issuer raised full-year guidance, but the margin gain rests on net price rather than volume.
Basis: calculation M9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Leverage is high on reported figures and moderate on adjusted ones, so the answer depends on which earnings measure holds. Reported net leverage of 7.73x, or 7.77x pro forma for the events since quarter end, falls to 4.81x without the goodwill impairment and to 4.04x for Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb on guided adjusted EBITDA, but cash interest cover was only 1.73x in FY2025 and cover for the last twelve months is not established.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Xifaxan is the dominant downside driver. It supplied 21.55% of FY2025 revenue and Salix earned 80.30% segment margin in nine months 2026; a loss of 37.78% of Xifaxan revenue would take Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb to 5.00x net leverage on guided EBITDA, and each 10% loss costs about USD 165 million of segment profit, against Medicare pricing from 2027 and expected generic competition in 2028.
Basis: calculation M7; calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

Liquidity is adequate through 2027 but thin against 2028 once the perimeters are separated. Group liquidity, cash plus undrawn facilities, of USD 3,620 million exceeds the USD 716 million due before the end of 2027, with pro forma liquidity after the 2027 redemption not established, yet Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb covers only 0.81x of the principal due through 2028 and Bausch + Lomb 0.80x, because each perimeter holds its own cash and facilities.
Basis: calculation M5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 127

Refinancing is the central risk and the structure makes it harder for unsecured holders. USD 3,766 million falls due in 2028, or 18.67% of principal, the issuer's ratings are Caa2 at Moody's and B- at S&P, and 68.28% of the Bausch + Lomb shares are pledged to the 126NumberCo secured creditors while non-guarantor subsidiaries produce 57.40% of revenue.
Basis: calculation M6; calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 131

Management is using cash to reduce debt rather than to distribute it, which supports creditors. It repurchased USD 602 million of 2026 notes in 2025, announced redemption of USD 643 million of 2027 notes from cash and has paid no dividend, while the USD 50 million buyback is small; against this the record of exchanges, including a 44.14% principal cut in 2022, shows willingness to re-rank claims under stress.
Basis: calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Capital intensity is low, which gives flexibility. Capex was 3.87% and research 6.13% of FY2025 revenue, and free cash flow reached USD 1,865 million over the last twelve months, but that is 49.43% of EBITDA excluding the impairment and is before USD 183 million of premium-related interest the issuer reports in financing.
Basis: calculation M4; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the issuer's guidance looks conservative: it implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 992 million to USD 1,092 million against USD 1,350 million in the third quarter, Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb reports fourteen consecutive quarters of growth, and leverage on guided adjusted EBITDA is between 4.04x and 4.16x in every perimeter. If Xifaxan held through 2028, or generic entry were delayed, the 2028 maturities would be refinanced from a stronger base and the view would improve. It would worsen if generic entry came earlier than expected, if Salix volumes kept falling while prices reset, or if a further exchange or release of the pledged shares re-ranked claims.
Basis: calculation M8; calculation M3; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Limitations

- Adjusted EBITDA is stated only for quarters and nine months, so the 4.16x and 4.04x leverage on guided adjusted EBITDA mix a forward management figure with year-end debt and could be too low if guidance is missed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4

- The covenant ratio the issuer reports, the covenant step-up date and the executed credit agreement are not supplied, so headroom against the 4.25x and 5.75x first-lien tests and the USD 400 million minimum liquidity is not established and the liquidity conclusion rests on balances only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Generic rifaximin launch timing and any settlement terms are not supplied, so the size and date of the Xifaxan loss are a reference level rather than an estimate and the downside view could be earlier or later.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

- Debt and cash are shown at the consolidated and perimeter levels the issuer prints, but no stand-alone cash flow statement for Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb is supplied, so free cash flow after interest for that perimeter is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 127

- The pro forma effect of the 2027 note redemption on net debt and cash is not established because the redemption price and accrued interest are not stated, so net leverage may differ slightly from the pro forma figures quoted.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: earnings and cash flow are improving at a pace that supports debt service. Adjusted EBITDA rose 29.55% and operating cash flow 89.39% in nine months 2026, so the cash that services USD 561 million of interest due in the fourth quarter is growing, although the gain rests on net price.
Basis: calculation M9; calculation M10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength: near-term liquidity covers the 2027 maturities and the issuer is retiring debt from cash. Group liquidity of USD 3,620 million exceeds the USD 716 million due before the end of 2027 and the redemption of USD 643 million of 2027 notes removes most of it, so the first call on refinancing is 2028.
Basis: calculation M5; calculation M12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength: capital intensity is low and there is no distribution to shareholders. Capex of 3.87% of revenue and research of 6.13% leave cash for debt, and no dividend has been paid since at least 2023, which keeps cash inside the group.
Basis: calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength: Bausch + Lomb is a growing, separately financed asset. It earned 27.04% of nine-month segment profit, its revenue grew 7% in the third quarter and it has refinanced its own debt to 2031, which gives a monetization option that would repay the 126NumberCo secured creditors first.
Basis: calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Weakness: earnings rest on one drug that is losing protection. Xifaxan is 21.55% of revenue, Salix earns an 80.30% margin on it, the Medicare price applies from 2027 and generic competition is expected in 2028, and a loss of 37.78% of Xifaxan revenue would take net leverage excluding Bausch + Lomb to 5.00x.
Basis: calculation M7; calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: the 2028 maturity wall meets that loss of protection. USD 3,766 million, or 18.67% of principal, falls due in 2028 and USD 4,482 million, or 22.22%, falls due by the end of 2028 from 2026, while Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb has only 0.81x cover through 2028.
Basis: calculation M5; calculation M6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness: reported leverage and interest cover are thin. Net leverage of 7.73x on reported EBITDA, or 7.77x pro forma for the events since quarter end, and 1.73x cash interest cover in FY2025 leave little room for an earnings miss, and the 4.81x figure without the impairment depends on adjusted earnings and issuer definitions.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness: structure and policy favor secured creditors over unsecured holders. The pledge covers 68.28% of the Bausch + Lomb shares held, non-guarantor subsidiaries produce 57.40% of revenue and the record of exchanges since 2022 shows claims being re-ranked under stress.
Basis: calculation M11; calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Confidence inputs

### Map: credit-risk transmission
| From | Relationship | Edge type | To | Evidence |
| Xifaxan generic entry | cuts Salix revenue and profit | Analyst Interpretation | Earnings excluding Bausch + Lomb | Salix margin 80.30%; Xifaxan 21.55% of revenue |
| Medicare price from 2027 | lowers the Xifaxan price | Documentary Fact | 2027 Salix revenue | 10-K: effective 2027-01-01 |
| Salix profit loss | raises leverage on a fixed debt base | Analyst Interpretation | Net leverage excluding B+L | 4.04x on guidance; 5.00x after a 37.78% loss |
| Higher leverage | weakens access to refinancing | Analyst Interpretation | USD 3,766m due in 2028 | Ratings Caa2 and B-; 2028 wall |
| Pledged Bausch + Lomb shares | sweep sale and dividend proceeds | Documentary Fact | 126NumberCo secured creditors | 10-Q: sweep above USD 50m of dividends |
| Bausch + Lomb cash | stays in Bausch + Lomb | Documentary Fact | Cash reaching Bausch Health | 10-Q: B+L cash generally not available |
| Redemption of 2027 notes | uses cash to cut debt | Documentary Fact | 2027 refinancing need | 10-Q: USD 643m on 2026-11-30 |
| Price-led Salix growth | exposes margin to price resets | Analyst Interpretation | Salix profit durability | 10-Q: price +504, volume -173 (USD m) |
| Exchanges and designations | re-rank claims when stressed | Analyst Interpretation | Unsecured recovery | 10-K: 2022 exchange cut principal 44.14% |
### Credit-relevant company description

Bausch Health is a Canadian-incorporated specialty pharmaceutical and device group whose revenue is half US-led specialty products and half Bausch + Lomb eye health, which gives scale and a branded portfolio but ties cash flow to a few franchises. Revenue was USD 10,266 million in FY2025 and USD 11,113 million over the last twelve months, the United States produced 59.79% of FY2025 revenue and three wholesalers took 48%, so cash flow visibility is good while products keep their protection and weak once one loses it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 342

The business model supports debt service because products are prescribed and reimbursed, but it concentrates refinancing confidence on Salix, whose segment profit was 47.34% of the nine-month total, and on Bausch + Lomb, whose cash is retained within it.
Basis: calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

No sponsor or controlling shareholder is disclosed, so the credit rests on operating cash flow and refinancing rather than owner support, and leverage tolerance is shown by behavior: no dividends, cash used to retire debt, and repeated liability management. The group holds about 87% of Bausch + Lomb through a restricted financing subsidiary, 126NumberCo, whose creditors have a first lien over the pledged shares, while the older secured and unsecured notes are not guaranteed by it, so claims on the largest subsidiary sit ahead of them. Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb share a chief executive in an interim role, which concentrates decisions on separation and dividends in one executive.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 138

Creditor alignment is mixed: change-of-control puts at 101% and covenant compliance support lenders, while the unrestricted status of Bausch + Lomb keeps its earnings and net debt out of the covenant tests and the 2022 exchange cut principal by 44.14% under troubled debt restructuring accounting.
Basis: calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable in volume but exposed to price and exclusivity, because growth is price-led and the largest product loses protection from 2027. Salix revenue rose USD 343 million in nine months 2026 on USD 504 million of net price against USD 173 million of lost volume after the exit of high-rebate channels, the Medicare price for Xifaxan applies from 2027-01-01 and generic competition is expected in 2028, so the price lever that lifted margins cannot be assumed to repeat and a drop in net price falls straight to profit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26
Outside Salix, International revenue grew 7.63% and Bausch + Lomb 8.58% in nine months 2026 and Diversified fell 1.03%, which diversifies growth but not the dependence of profit on Salix.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are improving because revenue is growing much faster than costs: nine-month revenue rose 11.34% while cost of goods sold rose 1.34% and selling, general and administrative costs rose 1.80%, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 34.34% to 39.95%. The large sales and marketing base is a fixed cost, so operating leverage cuts both ways, and a Xifaxan revenue loss would reduce profit by close to its revenue at the Salix margin, about USD 165 million for each 10% lost.
Basis: calculation M7; calculation M9; calculation M14; Financial foundation (CP-1)
Margins can be defended against cost inflation by the low capital need and research flexibility, but not against loss of exclusivity.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Cash conversion is moderate and improving but flattered by items reported outside operating cash flow. Free cash flow was USD 1,003 million in FY2025 and operating cash flow of USD 1,714 million less capex reached USD 1,462 million in nine months 2026 against USD 600 million, yet it is 49.43% of EBITDA excluding the impairment over the last twelve months, excludes USD 183 million of interest the issuer allocates to debt premiums, and bears USD 167 million of legacy legal settlement payments in nine months 2026.
Basis: calculation M4; calculation M16; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 27
Capex flexibility is limited to a small base of 3.87% of revenue, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA and on not paying distributions.
Basis: calculation M11
### Competitive forces

Rivalry and entry matter most through generic entrants: a generic rifaximin has final approval and exclusivity decisions are still being litigated, so entry pressure on Xifaxan is high and its timing is unconfirmed. Buyer power is high because three wholesalers took 48% of revenue and payers set prices through rebates of USD 1,377 million accrued at 2026-09-30 and Medicare negotiation; supplier power and the threat of substitutes are not established from the supplied documents.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58
### Policy, macro and regulatory factors

Policy factors are a primary credit driver because the Medicare negotiated price takes effect in 2027 and tariff rules changed in 2026; the issuer does not expect the tariff to be material. Economic exposure is mainly interest rates, as USD 6,615 million of debt is variable-rate and each 1 percentage point adds about USD 66 million of annual interest; social and technology factors are not primary drivers on the supplied evidence.
Basis: calculation M15; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93
### Credit-translated SWOT
- Strengths: improving earnings and cash, a nearly cleared 2027 wall, low capital intensity, no distributions and a separately financed Bausch + Lomb.
Basis: calculation M9; calculation M5
- Weaknesses: Xifaxan concentration, thin reported cover, a 2028 maturity wall and a structure that ranks unsecured holders behind 126NumberCo creditors.
Basis: calculation M6; calculation M11
- Opportunities: monetizing part of Bausch + Lomb, growth in Solta Medical in China and Bausch + Lomb, and a delay to generic entry.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
- Threats: generic launch in 2028, Medicare pricing, further exchanges that re-rank claims, antitrust and patent litigation and a Luxembourg tax assessment with no reserve.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality
The financial profile is average with a weak ability to refinance, and the nine dimensions are assessed as follows.
- Scale and market position is Average: revenue of USD 11,113 million over the last twelve months and a worldwide footprint, but the largest product is exposed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
- Competitive advantage is Average: patented products and device brands, with Xifaxan protection eroding.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
- Business diversification is Average: five segments, but 21.55% of revenue is one product, 59.79% is in one country and 48% goes through three customers.
Basis: calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A)
- Cost and capex flexibility is Average: capex is 3.87% of revenue and research 6.13%, but the sales base is fixed.
Basis: calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- Margin stability is Average: adjusted margin rose to 39.95% but on price rather than volume.
Basis: calculation M9; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- Free cash flow stability is Average: free cash flow moved from USD 1,260 million to USD 1,003 million and then to USD 1,865 million over the last twelve months.
Basis: calculation M4; calculation M16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Weak: ratings are Caa2 at Moody's and B- at S&P, USD 3,766 million falls due in 2028 and recent debt was secured at about 10.00% on the Bausch + Lomb shares.
Basis: calculation M6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-K_2025-12-31_bhc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 137
- Liquidity position is Average: group liquidity covers 2027 but each perimeter holds its own cash and facilities and cover through 2028 is 0.81x and 0.80x.
Basis: calculation M5; Financial foundation (CP-1)
- Financial policy and governance is Average: no distributions and debt reduction from cash, offset by high leverage tolerance and exchanges that re-ranked claims.
Basis: calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Credit supports are earnings momentum, low capital intensity and a cleared 2027 wall; constraints are concentration, the 2028 wall and structure; the trend is improving; key missing datapoints are the generic launch date, covenant ratios and executed debt documents.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is supportive for cash flow: guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 992 million to USD 1,092 million, the 2027 notes are being redeemed and no maturity above USD 701 million falls due before 2028, but 2027 brings the Medicare price and the pledged-share sweep terms limit what a Bausch + Lomb dividend can do for unsecured holders. Tailwinds are price, channel mix, Bausch + Lomb growth and the China distribution acquisition; headwinds are the 2027 price, litigation and the 2028 expiry.
Basis: calculation M8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4

Over three to five years the maturity profile is the dominant issue: USD 3,766 million in 2028, USD 1,667 million in 2029, USD 4,123 million in 2030, USD 3,896 million in 2031 and USD 6,000 million thereafter, so refinancing capacity depends on holding earnings after generic entry and on market windows.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Downside scenario

The downside path starts with generic rifaximin entering in or before 2028 after a lower Medicare price in 2027, which cuts Xifaxan volume and price. Salix, which earns an 80.30% margin, loses profit almost one for one, about USD 165 million for each 10% of Xifaxan revenue lost, so Bausch Health excluding Bausch + Lomb moves from 4.04x on guided adjusted EBITDA to 5.00x after a 37.78% loss, with net debt unchanged. That leverage arrives as USD 2,326 million of Bausch Health debt matures in 2028 and a further USD 1,639 million in 2029, so the first financial break is refinancing access rather than liquidity, because cash and facilities cover 2027.
Basis: calculation M3; calculation M7; calculation M11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bhc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128

Management has levers: the USD 643 million redemption shows cash can retire debt, capex of 3.87% and research of 6.13% can be cut, distributions are zero, and Bausch + Lomb could be monetized, with proceeds above USD 50 million swept to the 126NumberCo secured creditors first. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not established through 2028 without refinancing, and the primary downside path is generic Xifaxan competition meeting the 2028 maturities. Observable triggers are a Teva launch, falling Salix volume and any exchange offer.
Basis: calculation M11; calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Overall credit view

Overall, Bausch Health Companies Inc. presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by earnings momentum, a cleared 2027 wall and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on Xifaxan, thin reported cover and a 2028 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate near term and weak after 2027 because Xifaxan protection is ending. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding Salix earnings, the ratings, the pledged-share structure and market windows. The primary downside path is generic competition for Xifaxan meeting the 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require the generic launch date, the covenant ratios and the executed debt documents. Top risk: generic Xifaxan competition meeting the 2028 maturities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
